authors: Related Article | Research Policy The Career Effects of Scandal: Evidence from Scientific Retractions Pierre Azoulay
Joshua Lev Krieger We investigate how the scientific community's perception of a scientist's prior work changes when one of his articles is retracted. Relative to non-retracted control authors
faculty members who experience a retraction see the citation rate to their earlier
non-retracted articles drop by 10% on average
consistent with the Bayesian intuition that the market inferred their work was mediocre all along. We then investigate whether the eminence of the retracted author

the cause of the retraction (fraud vs. mistake) shape the magnitude of the penalty. We find that eminent scientists are more harshly penalized than their less distinguished peers in the wake of a retraction
but only in cases involving fraud or misconduct. When the retraction event had its source in “honest mistakes
” we find no evidence of differential stigma between high-
low-status faculty members. Keywords: Reputation ; Perception ; Status

papers.title: Developing Novel Drugs
authors: Read Now Related Working Paper | HBS Working Paper Series | 2017 Developing Novel Drugs Joshua Krieger
Dimitris Papanikolaou We analyze firms' decisions to invest in incremental
focusing specifically on pharmaceutical research. We develop a new measure of drug novelty that is based on the chemical similarity between new drug candidates
existing drugs. We show that drug candidates that we identify as ex-ante novel are riskier investments
in the sense that they are subsequently less likely to be approved by the FDA. However
more valuable―they are more clinically effective; have higher patent citations; lead to more revenue
to higher stock market value. Using variation in the expansion of Medicare prescription drug coverage
we show that firms respond to a plausibly exogenous cash flow shock by developing more molecularly novel drug compounds
as opposed to more so-called "me-too" drugs. This pattern suggests that
firms perceive novel drugs to be more valuable ex-ante investments
but that financial frictions may hinder their willingness to invest in these riskier candidates. Keywords: Research
